---
title: "Introduction to random forests in R"
date: "2020-01-04"
author: "Franz X. Mohr"
---


## Data

```{r}

library(dplyr)

set.seed(12345)

n <- 10000

# Raw data
data <- tibble(x1 = round(runif(n, 0, 1) * 100),
               x2 = runif(n, 2, 10),
               x3 = sample(0:1, n, replace = TRUE),
               y = factor(x1 > 50 & x2 <= 4))
```

## Estimation

### Obtain training sample

```{r}
n_train <- 1000

pos <- sample(1:n, n_train)

train <- data[pos, ]
```

### Estimate

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(randomForest)

rf <- randomForest(y ~ ., data = data)
```

## Results

```{r}
MDSplot(rf, data$y)
```

## References

Breiman, L. (2001), Random Forests, Machine Learning 45(1), 5-32.

Breiman, L (2002), “Manual On Setting Up, Using, And Understanding Random Forests V3.1”, https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~breiman/Using_random_forests_V3.1.pdf.
